newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar mauls mark, Eurobourses strong.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar mauls mark, Eurobourses strong.

text.p: The dollar rallied to a 34-month high against the mark on Tuesday on a combination of German jobs gloom and U.S. optimism, and the bulls came out of hiding on European equity markets, sending London, Frankfurt and Paris up more than one percent.

Sentiment on the stock markets, which had been heartened by Wall Street's higher close on Monday after three consecutive falls, was blunted slightly in mid-afternoon when the Dow opened flat and quickly fell a dozen or so points.
London and Paris slipped from their highs, but still remained firmly in positive territory, while Frankfurt's Dax index had already closed floor trading at a new record.

The dollar hit another 34-month high of 1.7138 marks in the European afternoon. Dollar bulls were given a boost by comments to the U.S. Budget Committee by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, who said inflation would be contained.

A key U.S. economic forecasting gauge, which posted its largest increase in eight months in January also helped the dollar by suggesting that economic growth would accelerate during the first half of the year, making an early U.S. rate hike more likely.

The Conference Board said its index of leading indicators -- designed to forecast economic activity six to nine months ahead -- rose 0.3 percent in January after a 0.1 percent gain in December. The January increase was the largest since a 0.3 percent rise last May.
Another key indicator, the U.S. February unemployment data, is due to be released at 1330 GMT on Friday.

"I think the belief in the market is that we're going to see a strong payroll report at the end of the week and thus an increased chance of a March 25 interest rate hike in the U.S.," said Tom Rayner, economist at Societe Generale in London.
Analysts reckon German unemployment, at a post-war record, means the Bundesbank is unlikely to raise interest rates in the near future, so keeping the dollar strong against the mark.
On Wall Street overnight the Dow Jones industrial average jumped 41.18 points to 6,918.92 after losing more than 160 points over the previous three sessions.

European bourses responded with relief. London shares started higher and the blue chip FTSE 100 index soon put on more than three-quarters of a percent, moving within 20 points of its all-time high of 4,362.4, set on 20 February. Shortly after Wall Street's open on Tuesday it was still up 40 points or nearly one percent.
"Rates are not going up in the UK before the election and a small rise in the U.S. will be taken in the market's stride," one dealer commented.

Provided Greenspan does not drop any bombshells in his testimony to a Congressional committee on Wednesday and the U.S. jobs data on Friday is in line with expectations, the FTSE could head up to the 4,400 level soon, dealers said.
In Frankfurt Germany's DAX index pushed up to close floor trading at a new record, having put on 1.74 percent during the session.

Dealers said the market had been boosted not only by Monday's Wall Street performance but also by the strength of the dollar -- which makes European exports more attractive -- and a rally in the car sector.
On the Paris bourse, too, the bulls were rampant during the day. By mid- afternoon the key CAC-40 index was off its highs but up around 1.8 percent.
Dealers said the market was well supported by a strong dollar had been expecting a higher Wall Street, but when the Dow opened flat and started to slip, French shares followed suit.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7100 marks and 121.95 yen, compared with 1.6941 and 120.92 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 42 points at 4,349.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 48.07 points at 2,649.15.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 56.8 points at 3,320.66.
PRECIOUS METALS Gold fixed at $361.75 compared with London's previous close of $362.25. Silver was at $5.26.
